D: Bruce Banner hides out in Brazil looking for a cure while the army hunts him down.
P: Serve the snacks when Bruce is working at the bottling plant in Rio.
S: the hillside favela in Rio de Janeiro

Crisp blistered pastry pockets stuffed with spiced beef mince, olives and egg, fried hot and served with a squeeze of lime and hot sauce. Brown 400g beef mince with 1 diced onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp paprika and salt, then stir in 50g chopped green olives and 2 chopped boiled eggs and cool. Cut 4 thawed puff or spring roll pastry sheets into 12cm squares. Put a spoonful of filling on each, fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork. Fry in oil at 180C for 3 minutes until blistered. Serve with lime and hot sauce.

Culver campus pepperoni and mushroom pizza
the pizzas Bruce uses to get past the guard at Culver

Thin crust blistered in a hot oven, topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella, pepperoni and garlic mushrooms, finished with chilli oil. Divide 1kg pizza dough into 4 and stretch thin. Spread each with 3 tbsp passata mixed with oregano and salt. Fry 200g sliced mushrooms in butter with 1 garlic clove. Top the bases with 400g grated mozzarella, 150g sliced pepperoni and the mushrooms. Bake on a hot tray at 250C for 10 minutes until blistered. Drizzle with chilli oil.
W: Bruce Banner hiding out in Brazil

Brazilian chocolate fudge balls of condensed milk, cocoa and butter, cooked thick, rolled by hand and coated in chocolate sprinkles. Put 395g condensed milk, 2 tbsp cocoa and 20g butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir constantly for about 10 minutes until it thickens and pulls away from the base in one mass. Tip onto a buttered plate and cool for 1 hour. With buttered hands, roll into 20 small balls, then roll in 100g chocolate sprinkles. Sit each in a small paper case.
K: the Brazilian bottling plant where Bruce works

Lime muddled with sugar and cachaça over crushed ice, topped with ice-cold guaraná soda, a nod to Bruce's job at the bottling plant. For each drink, cut half a lime into wedges and muddle hard in a glass with 2 tsp caster sugar. Fill with crushed ice, add 45ml cachaça and stir well. Top with about 60ml cold guaraná soda and stir once more. Make four, using 180ml cachaça in total. For a booze-free version, skip the cachaça and fill up with more guaraná.

s.how: Bring 250ml milk and 125ml oil to the boil and pour over 250g tapioca flour, mixing well. Cool slightly, then beat in 2 eggs and 100g grated parmesan to a sticky dough. Roll into balls and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.

s.note: the green giant smashing everything in his way
s.how: Halve 3 ripe avocados and smash roughly with a fork, leaving it chunky. Stir in the juice of 2 limes, chopped coriander, a finely diced red onion, a chopped green chilli and salt. Serve straight away with warm corn chips.

m.note: Bruce working his way through Brazil
m.how: Grill 800g rump steak over high heat and rest. Toast 200g cassava flour in 60g butter until golden and nutty. Chop tomatoes with onion and red wine vinegar for a vinaigrette. Slice the steak and serve with farofa, warm black beans and the vinaigrette.
